==Accidents and notable incidents==
{{Main|List of accidents and incidents involving the Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II}}

The F-35 is a statistically safe military aircraft, described as being twice as safe as the F-16.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-04 |title=An F-35 Went Down in New Mexico. It's Still One of the Safest Planes in the Skies. |url=https://www.popularmechanics.com/military/aviation/a60962511/f-35-went-down-in-new-mexico/ |access-date=2024-06-15 |website=Popular Mechanics |language=en-US}}</ref> Still, since 2014, more than a dozen have crashed or otherwise been involved in incidents that have killed or severely injured people or destroyed the aircraft. Some were caused by operator error; others by mechanical problems, some of which set the entire program back.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marrow |first=Michael |date=2024-06-05 |title=What a crashed jet means for an F-35 program already thin on test planes |url=https://breakingdefense.com/2024/06/what-a-crashed-jet-means-for-an-f-35-program-already-thin-on-test-planes/ |access-date=2024-06-15 |website=Breaking Defense |language=en-US}}</ref>

{{As of|2026|8}}, there were 12 crashes causing the loss of an F-35 airframe, primarily in the US.<ref name=":20" />

The only known fatal crash of an F-35 occurred on 9 April 2019, when a [[Japan Air Self-Defense Force]] F-35A crashed in the Pacific Ocean east of [[Aomori Prefecture]] at an estimated speed of Mach 0.9.<ref name=":20" /> The accident report attributed the cause to the pilot's [[spatial disorientation]]. The pilot's remains and the flight recorder were salvaged, although no data could be retrieved, while the wreckage itself was not salvaged.<ref name="spatial disorientation" />

On 31 July 2026, a US Marine Corps F-35B crashed and was destroyed at [[Marine Corps Air Station Miramar]] in San Diego, California. The pilot ejected safely.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shelbourne |first1=Mallory |title=BREAKING: F-35B Crashes Near Marine Corps Air Station Miramar |url=https://news.usni.org/2026/07/31/breaking-f-35b-crashes-near-marine-corps-air-station-miramar |website=USNI News |access-date=1 August 2026 |date=31 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Paoletto |first1=Isabella |title=F-35 jet 'mishap' on San Diego Marine base, pilot ejected |url=https://fox5sandiego.com/news/local-news/smoke-fire-mcas-miramar/ |website=FOX 5 San Diego |access-date=1 August 2026 |date=31 July 2026 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Cooper |first1=Aaron |title=Military F-35B fighter jet crashes and burns at California Marine Corps base |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/07/31/us/military-jet-crash-california-marine-base |website=CNN |access-date=1 August 2026 |date=31 July 2026}}</ref>

=== 2026 Iran war ===
On 19 March 2026, during the [[2026 Iran war]], a US F-35 flying a combat mission over Iran was forced to make an emergency landing at a regional air base.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Melimopoulos |first=Elizabeth |title=US F-35 aircraft makes emergency landing after a combat mission over Iran |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/19/us-f-35-aircraft-makes-emergency-landing-after-a-combat-mission-over-iran |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref> The [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] said it had "seriously damaged" the F-35.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |title=Iran says it struck US F-35 over central Iran, with fighter jet's fate unclear |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/iran-says-it-struck-us-f-35-over-central-iran-with-fighter-jets-fate-unclear/3872032 |access-date=2026-03-21 |website=www.aa.com.tr}}</ref><ref name=":15">{{Cite web |title=Iran video said to show US F-35 being hit |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/3/20/iran-video-said-to-show-us-f-35-being-hit |access-date=2026-03-21 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref> It was the first time an F-35 sustained damage from enemy fire since it was deployed in combat in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shankar |first=Priyanka |date=23 March 2026 |title=Has Iran brought down an 'unkillable' US F-35 jet? |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/23/has-iran-brought-down-an-unkillable-us-f-35-jet |access-date=2026-08-02 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref> It was also the first Iranian interception of any US aircraft.<ref name=":16">{{Cite web |date=2026-03-19 |title=US fighter jet makes emergency landing after being hit by Iranian fire |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/iran-hits-us-plane-emergency-landing-b2941974.html |access-date=2026-03-21 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> The aircraft landed safely.<ref name=":13" />

On 15 September 2026, the [[Congressional Budget Office]] published the report "Estimating the Cost of Combat Operations Against Iran", which listed an F-35A "battle loss" which it estimated could be repaired for $50 million or replaced for the original unit cost of $120 million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Estimating the Cost of Combat Operations Against Iran |url=https://www.cbo.gov/publication/62756 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260915213303/https://www.cbo.gov/publication/62756 |archive-date=15 September 2026 |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=Congressional Budget Office |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

== UK F-35 exports to Israel and legal challenge ==
The United Kingdom's participation in the F-35 program became the subject of political and legal controversy during the [[2025 Gaza War|Gaza war]]. In September 2024, the British government suspended 29 arms export licenses after concluding that there was a clear risk that the items concerned might be used to commit or facilitate serious violations of international humanitarian law in Gaza. Licenses supplying components to the multinational F-35 program were exempted where the government could not identify Israel as the final end user. Ministers argued that suspending all UK supplies to the program would disrupt the global F-35 supply chain and have serious consequences for the defense of the United Kingdom, NATO allies and other international partners.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-02 |title=UK suspends around 30 arms export licences to Israel for use in Gaza over International Humanitarian Law concerns |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-suspends-around-30-arms-export-licences-to-israel-for-use-in-gaza-over-international-humanitarian-law-concerns |access-date=2026-07-13 |website=UK Government}}</ref>

The Palestinian human rights organization [[Al-Haq]] challenged the F-35 exemption in judicial review proceedings. In June 2025, the [[UK High Court]] dismissed the challenge. The court noted that the structure of the multinational program meant that F-35 aircraft supplied to Israel would contain UK-manufactured components, but held that the central question involved the government's continued participation in a multilateral defense program regarded by ministers as vital to national and international security. It concluded that this "acutely sensitive and political issue" was for the executive, accountable to Parliament and the electorate, rather than the courts.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-30 |title=UK court rejects Palestinian NGO's case over F-35 parts to Israel |url=https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/society-equity/uk-export-f-35-parts-israel-was-lawful-court-rules-2025-06-30/ |access-date=2026-07-13 |website=Reuters}}</ref>

Al-Haq sought to appeal the ruling, arguing that the exemption was incompatible with the UK's international law obligations and its own arms-export controls. In November 2025, the [[Court of Appeal (England and Wales)|Court of Appeal]] refused permission for a further appeal, leaving the F-35 exemption in place.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-12 |title=The King (On the application of Al-Haq) v. The Secretary of State for Business and Trade |url=https://www.judiciary.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Al-Haq-v-SSBT-Approved-judgment-PDF-format.pdf/ |access-date=2026-07-13 |website=High Court of England and Wales}}</ref>
